prompt: What question did Renata ask in every conversation to build the list of stakeholders for the CT-e service?
hint: It found support and the accounting firm.

choices.text: Who is invited to the planning meeting?
choices.why: The planning meeting is where the list started too short; three stakeholders were missing from it.

choices.text: Who has the most senior title in each area?
choices.why: Seniority finds the high-power corner and misses the people who meet the system when it fails.

choices.text: Who gets the phone call when this fails?
choices.why: Right: it reaches past the planners to support, the accountants and the certificate nobody owned.

choices.text: Which teams will call the new service's API?
choices.why: That finds Matching and Tracking and misses finance, product and the drivers.

prompt: Why does the lesson treat SEFAZ differently from the other ten stakeholders of the CT-e service?
hint: It will not attend a meeting.

choices.text: Its interest is low, so it belongs in the monitor corner
choices.why: SEFAZ decides whether every CT-e is valid; low interest is not the issue.

choices.text: A constraint to plan for, not someone to persuade
choices.why: Right: its rules, outages and layout changes shape the design, and somebody owns following them.

choices.text: Government bodies are outside the architect's work
choices.why: The opposite: its technical notes are part of the architect's reading for this service.

choices.text: It is the accounting firm's concern and not Carreto's
choices.why: The firm files obligations; the service that talks to SEFAZ is Carreto's.

prompt: Match each corner of the power and interest grid to its standard instruction.
hint: Power decides whether they can stop it; interest decides how closely they watch.

prompt: The drivers sit in the keep-informed corner of Renata's grid, though the CT-e service exists for them. How does the lesson read that?
hint: What the quadrants are instructions about.

choices.text: They matter less because they are paid by the trip
choices.why: Being paid by the trip makes a delay cost them more, not matter less.

choices.text: They should be moved to manage closely and invited to the fortnightly meeting
choices.why: None of them sits in Carreto's meetings; their view arrives another way.

choices.text: The corner is about effort, and their view arrives through Diego and support
choices.why: Right: the grid sets how much contact, not how much the person counts.

choices.text: They are not stakeholders, as they are not employees
choices.why: Anybody affected by the decision is a stakeholder, employee or not.

prompt: In July SEFAZ published the date for the new CT-e layout. What did Renata change?
hint: The grid moves.

choices.text: She met Sílvio weekly instead of every two weeks
choices.why: Right: his interest rose with a date that could stop trucks, so the contact rose with it until the layout was live.

choices.text: Nothing, so that the grid stayed stable for everybody
choices.why: A grid drawn once is wrong within a month; the lesson asks for a redraw at each phase.

choices.text: She moved Sílvio to the monitor corner, since finance was settled
choices.why: His interest went up, not down.

choices.text: She sent Sílvio the architecture diagram of the service
choices.why: Only Bruno would read one; Sílvio needed the risk in reais and the date.

prompt: By the lesson, which stakeholders are missed most often when an initiative is planned?
hint: Little power, direct knowledge.

choices.text: Executives above the sponsor
choices.why: They are rarely forgotten; their power makes them visible.

choices.text: The developers writing the code
choices.why: They are in the planning meeting from the start.

choices.text: Those who meet the system when it fails
choices.why: Right: support, on-call, an outside party who files or audits: little power over the design, the most direct knowledge of what goes wrong.

choices.text: Product managers of neighbouring areas
choices.why: They show up in quarterly planning; they are not the group the lesson names.

prompt: How does the lesson divide the work between product and the architect?
hint: What, why, in what order; and the structural how.

choices.text: The architect sets priorities whenever they affect the structure
choices.why: Priority is product's; the architect brings the structural cost to that decision.

choices.text: Product owns what and why; the architect, the structural how
choices.why: Right: neither decides the trade-off alone, and product decides it with the consequences on the table.

choices.text: Product decides everything and the architect implements it
choices.why: That is the yes-to-everything failure: the structure absorbs every cost silently.

choices.text: They vote, with the CTO breaking ties
choices.why: No vote in the lesson; ownership of the consequence decides.

prompt: The Shipper team estimated the "number of trucks" field at a week. Why was the real cost much higher?
hint: One load, one of everything.

choices.text: The form framework could not add a field
choices.why: The form was the cheap part.

choices.text: The law forbids several trucks on one load
choices.why: The law asks for one CT-e per truck, which both options respect.

choices.text: Five teams had built on one load meaning one truck
choices.why: Right: driver, CT-e, payout, tracking session and invoice line all assumed it.

choices.text: Pricing had no formula for grain loads
choices.why: Grain is an ordinary load for Pricing; the problem was the count of trucks.

prompt: Option B needed five teams for 11 weeks. Counting one team-week per team per week, how many team-weeks is that?
hint: Teams times weeks.

prompt: Helena chose option A, linked loads. Why does the lesson call that a good outcome?
hint: It is not about A being right in general.

choices.text: A was cheaper, and keeping cost down is the architect's goal
choices.why: The lesson says plainly it was not good because A was right in general.

choices.text: Renata had recommended A from the start
choices.why: Renata gave options, not a verdict.

choices.text: B would have broken the rule of one CT-e per truck
choices.why: B keeps one CT-e per truck too.

choices.text: She saw the costs, and a trigger settles when to revisit
choices.why: Right: the owner of the priority decided with eleven weeks and the reporting problem in front of her, and 300 a month says when to revisit.

prompt: Why does Renata take part in product discovery and not only in quarterly planning?
hint: What can still change at each moment?

choices.text: Discovery is where the budget for each feature is approved
choices.why: Budgets are not the point; the shape of the feature is.

choices.text: By planning the shape is fixed, so she only prices it
choices.why: Right: two weeks earlier a question about the one-to-one still had room to change what gets built.

choices.text: Product needs an engineer to supervise its interviews
choices.why: She is there for the structural question, not to supervise.

choices.text: Architects are kept out of planning meetings at Carreto
choices.why: Nothing says so; she attends both.

prompt: SAFe calls the structural work that keeps the next features cheap the architectural ___.
hint: A word from airports.

prompt: Helena would store a shipment as one record with a list of trucks; Renata would store each leg as its own record. By the lesson's test, whose call is it?
hint: Ask whose consequence it is.

choices.text: Renata's: the cost lands on the structure
choices.why: Right: how a shipment is modelled is on Renata's side of the line, and she says so.

choices.text: Tomás's, because the two disagree
choices.why: Escalating every disagreement makes the CTO the decider of everything.

choices.text: Helena's, because the feature and its customers are hers
choices.why: The feature is hers; how it is modelled lands on the structure.

choices.text: The Shipper team's, by a vote of its engineers
choices.why: No vote in the lesson; the test is whose consequence it is.

prompt: Which statement is Conway's law, as the lesson paraphrases it?
hint: Melvin Conway, 1968.

choices.text: A system grows until it fills the teams available to build it
choices.why: That is closer to a joke about work expanding; Conway's point is about structure.

choices.text: A design copies the communication structure of whoever designs it
choices.why: Right: the organisation's lines of communication reappear as the system's boundaries.

choices.text: Each module should have a single owning team
choices.why: That is a conclusion Carreto drew from the law, not the law.

choices.text: Teams should be sized by the number of services they run
choices.why: The law says nothing about team size.

prompt: Six of nine incidents in invoicing began between Shipper and Payments. What was Renata's inverse Conway proposal?
hint: Decide the structure, then arrange the teams.

choices.text: Give the module to one team, behind an interface
choices.why: Right: one team changes it, one is on call, and the seam becomes an interface.

choices.text: Freeze changes to invoicing until a rewrite
choices.why: Freezing stops the incidents by stopping the work.

choices.text: Merge Shipper and Payments into one team
choices.why: One team twice the size would own too much, and cognitive load is the other half of the book.

choices.text: Split invoicing in two, one half per team
choices.why: That keeps the seam inside invoicing, where the incidents were.

prompt: Renata proposed moving invoicing work to Payments. Why did she not move the two developers' work herself?
hint: Whose decision is it?

choices.text: She was busy with the CT-e service
choices.why: Time was not the reason the lesson gives.

choices.text: Team Topologies says architects may not change teams
choices.why: The book says nothing like that.

choices.text: Payments had refused to take invoicing over
choices.why: Payments took it over within a quarter.

choices.text: Moving work between teams is a decision for their managers
choices.why: Right: her part was the argument and the interface; the managers' part was the organisation.

prompt: Match each Team Topologies type to its example at Carreto.
hint: Flow, internal services, specialist knowledge, help that leaves.

pairs.right: Driver, owning the drivers' app end to end
Pricing, with freight pricing and the ANTT floor
Renata's three weeks with the Driver team
the team that runs the pipeline and the service template

prompt: How does the lesson measure whether Renata's enabling work with the Driver team succeeded?
hint: The fourth week.

choices.text: Her name is on the team's ADR as approver
choices.why: Approval turns facilitation into a dependency.

choices.text: The team stopped needing her
choices.why: Right: by the fourth week Diego's team made the decisions without her.

choices.text: She wrote the offline design herself
choices.why: She explicitly did not write it for them.

choices.text: She stayed with the team until the app shipped
choices.why: Staying is the gatekeeper pattern lesson 17 warns about.

prompt: Put a proposal's path through Carreto's architecture forum in order.
hint: Tuesday, then Thursday, then the ADR.
items: A draft ADR is posted by Tuesday
People read the draft before the meeting
The 45 minutes on Thursday go to questions and advice
The advice and what was done with it go into the ADR
trap: The forum does not approve; deciding before hearing the advice skips the reason it exists.

prompt: Why does the forum give advice instead of approving proposals?
hint: What teams learn to bring to a board that approves.

choices.text: Approval draws decisions already made; advice draws them early
choices.why: Right: early is when advice is most useful, and the forum heard 23 proposals in six months.

choices.text: Advice is quicker to write down in the ADR
choices.why: The recording is the same either way; the effect on teams is the reason.

choices.text: Approving would need a quorum that the twelve people present cannot form
choices.why: Numbers in the room are not the reason given.

choices.text: An architect has no authority to approve anything
choices.why: Lesson 3 gives authority more than one source; the forum's design is about the teams.

prompt: Renata starts a new initiative: paying drivers by Pix within an hour of the delivery proof. Which steps match this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: The list, the grid, and the grid moving.

choices.text: Ask in each conversation who gets the phone call when it fails
choices.why: Yes: that is how support and the certificate were found last time.

choices.text: Send every stakeholder the same weekly email, to be fair
choices.why: Same message, same rhythm for all is the second wrong picture the lesson opens with.

choices.text: Place each stakeholder on the grid and pick a contact rhythm per corner
choices.why: Yes: the corner sets how much attention each one gets.

choices.text: Redraw the grid when the work changes phase
choices.why: Yes: interest moves with dates and launches.

choices.text: Leave support out until launch, as they have little power
choices.why: Support meets the system when it fails; an hour with them early is cheap.

prompt: After the CT-e service went live, Helena's interest dropped back to one step of the shipper flow. What does the lesson suggest about the fortnightly meeting with her?
hint: Change it, and how.

choices.text: Keep it, since stopping would look like a loss of interest
choices.why: A meeting with nothing in it is a cost to her.

choices.text: Stop it quietly, since she will not notice
choices.why: Changing silently is exactly what reads as being dropped.

choices.text: Meet her monthly instead, and tell her that is the change
choices.why: Right: redraw the grid and say so, or the change reads as being dropped.

choices.text: Hand the meeting over to Bruno
choices.why: Bruno's stake is invoicing, not Helena's flow.

prompt: A new team now owns the CT-e service, and Shipper still edits the service's templates directly in its code, "just this once". Which interaction mode should the two teams move to?
hint: The mode the invoicing change moved to.

choices.text: Collaboration, kept permanently
choices.why: A permanent, accidental collaboration is how invoicing produced six incidents.

choices.text: Facilitating, with Shipper teaching the new team
choices.why: Nothing here is a capability to teach; it is an ownership seam.

choices.text: X-as-a-service, through an interface the owner maintains
choices.why: Right: Shipper asks for templates through the service's interface and stops editing them.

choices.text: Shipper becomes the platform team for the CT-e service
choices.why: That moves ownership back to the team that should give it up.
